content: {"id": "76398335-d741-4021-b021-c51fa36d518c", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Our application gets AccessDeniedException when it calls InvokeModel on Bedrock. Is this something we can fix in our IAM policy, or is it coming from somewhere else?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "a57aea6c-7fe2-4b76-a06f-f864e6c4523a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "It could be your IAM policy, but IAM isn't the only possible source. The full error message usually tells you which one it is.

**Reading the message**
- **"...is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource ... because no identity-based policy allows..."**: Your caller's role or user is missing the permission. You can fix this in IAM.
- **"...with an explicit deny in a service control policy"** or **"...permissions boundary"**: The block is above or around your IAM policy. An Organizations SCP or a permissions boundary is denying the call, so adding an Allow to the role won't help. Someone with Organizations access has to change the SCP.
- **"...with an explicit deny in an identity-based policy"**: One of your own policies has a Deny, such as a region condition or a model restriction. You can fix this in IAM.
- **Messages about model access, a subscription, or an agreement**: This isn't an IAM policy problem. The model may not be enabled in that account and region. Third-party models can also require an AWS Marketplace subscription, which needs `aws-marketplace:Subscribe` and `ViewSubscriptions` on whoever enables it.

**Common IAM-side causes**
- **Resource ARN mismatch.** If you call through a cross-region inference profile (model IDs prefixed with `us.`, `eu.`, and so on), the policy has to allow the inference-profile ARN. It also has to allow the underlying foundation-model ARNs in every region the profile can route to. Allowing only one region's `foundation-model/...` ARN is a frequent cause.
- **Wrong region.** The model may not be available or enabled in the region your app calls.
- **Streaming.** If you use `InvokeModelWithResponseStream`, you need `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` as well.
- **VPC endpoint policy.** If you reach Bedrock through a VPC endpoint, its policy can deny the call.

If you paste the full error message, with the account ID and ARNs redacted if you like, I can narrow down which of these it is. If you give me the calling role and region, I can also check the role's policies in the connected account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
